case_name: Sh. Jitender Kumar Sharma vs State & Another

parties.respondent_defendant: State and another, parents and authorities

facts_of_case: Minors Jitender and Poonam eloped and got married without informing their families. Poonam's family opposed the marriage. The couple was apprehended and sent to separate facilities.

legal_principles.principle: A marriage solemnized in contravention of clause (iii) of Section 5 of the HMA is neither void nor voidable.
legal_principles.held: This view has been reinforced in Ravi Kumar v. The State: 124 (2005) DLT 1 (DB) and Manish Singh v. State Govt of NCT: AIR 2006 Del 37= 126 DLT 28 (DB).
cited_cases: Ravi Kumar v. The State: 124 (2005) DLT 1 (DB)
Manish Singh v. State Govt of NCT: AIR 2006 Del 37= 126 DLT 28 (DB)
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — significance in determining the validity of a Hindu marriage

legal_principles.principle: The legislature's intention is crucial in determining the validity of a Hindu marriage.
legal_principles.held: If the legislature had intended that such a marriage would be void or invalid, it could have easily included clause (iii) of section 5 in Section 11 itself.
cited_cases: Ravi Kumar v. The State: 124 (2005) DLT 1 (DB)
Manish Singh v. State Govt of NCT: AIR 2006 Del 37= 126 DLT 28 (DB)
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — significance in determining the legislative intent behind a Hindu marriage

outcome.final_order: The court allowed the appeal and did not register a case against Jitender and Poonam.
